How It Works

The Pipeline

CamerasTwo or more angles — close on the action, wide on everything
SwitcherEvery camera plugs into it — it picks which shot the world sees, one tap
ComputerTakes the switcher's picture and sends it out live to the internet

Cameras → switcher → computer. That's the spine of every livestream on earth.

LOGO
The Part Everyone Forgets

Audio Rides
Its Own Road

Not the CameraCamera mics hear the room — echoey and far away. The soundboard feeds the stream directly.
The DelayVideo takes longer to process than audio — they arrive out of sync
Your JobLine them up — half a second off and the lips don't match. Everyone notices.

The Camera Operator's Job

Stay On
The Action

The RuleA stream is only as good as its shot — if the action moves and you don't, the internet watches an empty stage
The SafetyOne camera always stays wide — framed to catch everything, no matter what happens
The SaveWhen a close shot loses the moment, the director cuts wide — the boring camera saves the broadcast
LOGO
Framing, In 60 Seconds

Make the Shot
Look Right

ThirdsEyes near the top third of the frame — not dead center. Center feels like a mugshot.
HeadroomA little space above the head — a little. A forehead cut off is better than a foot of empty ceiling.
Room to MoveFrame wide enough that one step doesn't escape you — tight is pretty; wide is safe
